marks.english: Seal-script square 景德鎮製 mark of the 1950s (and its 1970s revival)
marks.description: Square seal-script mark, usually overglaze red or blue (underglaze blue on blue-and-white); early examples on the national blue-and-white 'haitang' pattern.
marks.what_it_is: A four-character seal-script square mark 'made in Jingdezhen' used by state and research units in the early PRC; one source narrows the first form to c. 1954–55 and records a redrawn version late in the Cultural Revolution and a revival after 1976.

periods.label: First seal form
periods.note: one source: not before 1954, not after end-1955

periods.label: Redrawn seal
periods.note: late Cultural Revolution, strokes less even

marks.dating_value: Places a piece in the PRC era. Distinguishing the 1950s seal from the 1970s redrawing depends on stroke quality (single source). Gotheborg dates plain 景德鎮製 marks from c. 1950 to the 1990s, so the mark by itself is a broad PRC indicator only.
marks.later_copies: Redrawn by factories in the 1970s; the plain mark is still used (Gotheborg examples bought new in 1992).
marks.notes: The brief asked for a 'green 1950s–60s 景德鎮製 seal'; neither source here confirms green for the four-character 景德鎮製 seal. Green is recorded for the six-character 中國景德鎮製 seal (prc-zhongguo-jingdezhen-zhi-seal).

facts.claim: The seal-script square 景德鎮製 appeared soon after 1949, probably not before 1954 nor after end-1955; not a private-firm design; first on blue-and-white haitang wares.

marks.dating_value: 九江陶校 marks date to 1934 until the school moved away in the war (c. 1938).

facts.claim: The Jiangxi Porcelain Company set up its branch and a ceramic school at Gaomen, Poyang; after 1911 the school became provincial and separate from the company.

sources.name: 《景德镇市志》第二卷（中国瓷都·景德镇市瓷业志）第七篇, 第三章, 第二节 官办瓷厂: 江西瓷业公司 (景德镇市地方志办公室; PDF on jdz.gov.cn)
sources.says: 分厂设鄱阳（城内高门）…在分厂中附建一陶业学堂…1911年以后…陶业学堂改为江西省立，从此江西瓷业公司与陶业学堂分开

sources.name: Gotheborg.com, 'Chinese Jingdezhen porcelain after 1949 / 20th century Chinese porcelain factories' (J.-E. Nilsson; based on documents sourced in Jingdezhen 1990 and 1992)
sources.says: Soon after the company established a ceramics school at Gaomen in Poyang, Raozhou.

facts.claim: School names: 1912 江西省立饒州陶業學校; 1915 甲種工業學校; 1927 江西省立陶業學校; 1934 moved to Jiujiang as 江西省立九江陶瓷職業學校; 1944 to Jingdezhen; 1947 陶瓷專科學校. 九江陶校 marks therefore 1934 to before the war-time move.

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 1934年由鄱阳迁九江，改名为江西省立九江陶瓷职业学校。抗战期间，校址先后迁靖安、萍乡等地…凡落“九江陶校”字样款识的器物，均为1934年至抗战前九江生产

marks.english: 浮梁陶職 / 浮梁縣陶校製 — Fuliang county ceramic vocational school (1931–44)
marks.description: Iron-red seal script in a double square: 浮梁縣陶校製 or 浮梁陶職.
marks.what_it_is: Marks of the Fuliang county porcelain-decoration vocational school, founded 1931, merged into the provincial school in 1944.
marks.dating_value: Dates a piece to 1931–1944.

facts.claim: Founded 1931 (浮梁縣立飾瓷科職業學校), renamed 1935, merged 1944; examples dated 1937 and 1939.

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 浮梁陶职 全称为浮梁县立饰瓷科职业学校，1931年成立…1944年与江西省立陶瓷职业学校合并…故书浮梁陶职款识的器物应为193l—1944年间生产

marks.english: 勝利瓷業公司 / 勝利公司 'Victory Porcelain Company' (after 1945)
marks.description: Red seal 勝利公司 (sometimes gilt), or regular script 勝利瓷業公司.
marks.what_it_is: Republic porcelain company whose marks appear on wares inscribed after the 1945 victory; also on work by Zhang Peixuan.
marks.dating_value: 1945–49 (not after 1949 according to the source).

facts.claim: Wares inscribed 乙酉冬月 (1945) and work by Zhang Peixuan carry the mark; company post-1945 and pre-PRC.

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 当是在1945年抗战胜利之后…该公司亦不会成立于建国后，因张沛轩的作品落有该公司款识

marks.english: 華昌公司 / 江西華昌出品 (1930s)
marks.description: Stamped 江西華昌出品.
marks.what_it_is: Republic company whose recorded products include a service for Chiang Kai-shek (蔣 in red seal script) and a 1935 eggshell cup.

facts.claim: Huachang company made a service marked 蔣 for Chiang Kai-shek; a cup stamped 江西華昌出品 is inscribed 廿四年 (1935).

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 华昌公司 沿革不详，从传世晶来看，见有为蒋介石生产的餐具…“江西华昌出品”…廿四年为公元1935年

marks.english: 江西桐華公司 / 桐華居 (early 20th century)
marks.description: Ink regular script 江西桐華公司 or red seal 桐華公司.
marks.what_it_is: Small Republic company; 桐華公司 base marks occur with 桐華居 written on the side.
marks.dating_value: Early 20th century to the 1920s (based on dated 桐華居 pieces).

facts.claim: Wares with 桐華居 dates are early 20th century to the 1920s; if the same firm, 桐華公司 and 桐華居 are one.

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 如果该公司即为江西桐华公司，那么与桐华居即为一家，而从其它落桐华居款器物的年款上看，则生产活动当在20世纪初至20年代

marks.english: 江西利生公司 / 利生工廠 (by c. 1920)
marks.description: Ink inscription 利生公司作 with cyclical date.
marks.what_it_is: Republic company; one tray inscribed 1923; a 'modern beauty' plaque with 利生工廠.
marks.dating_value: Not later than 1923; possibly by 1920.

facts.claim: A tray inscribed 癸亥年仲春利生公司作 (1923); 利生工廠 may be the same firm, which would put it by 1920.

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 时在癸亥年仲舂利生公司作…为1923年作品…其成立的时间当不会晚于1920年

marks.english: 竹裏館 / 竹裏瓷社 (1910s–20s)
marks.description: Underglaze blue 景鎮竹裏館出品 in a begonia-shaped double ring; or 竹裏瓷社; ink 竹裏館作 on the side.
marks.what_it_is: Jingdezhen shop (also 竹裏瓷社) active in the 1910s–20s, selling hat stands and vases with costume-lady figures to a broad market.

facts.claim: Active 1910s–20s; a hat stand inscribed 甲子 (1924) 竹裏館作.

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 竹里馆出品 亦称竹里瓷社，从器物外壁题款看，20世纪10-20年代较为活跃…“甲子秋月竹里馆作”，为1924年作品

marks.english: 松雲軒 (杨記) shop mark (1910–20s)
marks.description: Oval seal 松雲軒 with outer legend 楊記…改良名瓷; or red 松雲軒造 in double square.
marks.what_it_is: Jingdezhen shop run by a Yang (楊記), 'improved famous porcelain'; hat stands with figures dated 1920–21.
marks.dating_value: 1910s–early 1920s.

facts.claim: Hat stands dated 庚申 (1920) and 辛酉 (1921); owner surnamed Yang.

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 松云轩 生产年代约为1910—1920年…外为“杨记，西发XX改良名瓷”字样。由此推知店主为杨姓…为1920年作品…为1921年产品

marks.english: 碧玉軒造 shop mark (1920s)
marks.description: Red seal 碧玉軒造 in a circle; ink 碧玉軒寫.
marks.what_it_is: Jingdezhen shop of the 1920s making famille rose costume-lady teapots and hat stands.

facts.claim: Examples inscribed 庚申 (1920) and 辛酉 (1921).

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 碧玉轩造 生产年代约在20世纪20年代…为1921年产品…为1920年产品

marks.english: 鑫源軒造 shop mark (1920s)
marks.description: Red stamped seal 鑫源軒造.
marks.what_it_is: Decorating shop whose red seal base mark appears on 1920s hat stands painted by Wu Shaofeng.
marks.notes: Both facts come from the same book (Tieyuan & Ximing), so only one independent source.

facts.claim: Wu Shaofeng's hat stands and teapots usually have the red stamp 鑫源軒造; one dated 壬戌 (1922).

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（五）人名款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 7 pages)
sources.says: 吴少峰 创作活动约在20世纪20年代左右…底多为红彩戳印“鑫源轩造”…“壬戌夏月昌江客次吴少峰写”

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 鑫源轩造 以美术彩绘为主…为吴少峰所绘，底红彩印章款“鑫源轩造”

marks.english: 江西義成公司 / 胡義成出品
marks.description: Underglaze blue two-line regular script 江西義成公司.
marks.what_it_is: Republic firm known mainly from famille rose hat stands, marked in underglaze blue on the base with 胡義成出品 in ink on the side.
marks.dating_value: Republic period (hat-stand era).

facts.claim: Famille rose hat stands with blue two-line 江西義成公司 base mark and ink 胡義成出品 on the side.

sources.name: 铁源、溪明,《民国瓷器鉴定》, 民国瓷器款识（四）厂店款 (reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2005-02-28, 4 pages)
sources.says: 江西义成公司 产品以粉彩帽筒最为常见，款字多为青花双行楷款，器物外壁多墨书“胡义成出品”

marks.english: 湖南瓷業公司 Hunan Porcelain Company, Liling (1906–1930)
marks.description: Incised or painted company marks; a Hunan Museum vase is incised with the company name and Xuantong 2nd year (1910).
marks.what_it_is: Company founded at Liling, Hunan, with the Hunan Porcelain School, on the initiative of Xiong Xiling; developed Liling underglaze polychrome (釉下五彩), gold medal at the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition.
marks.dating_value: A Hunan Porcelain Company mark dates a piece to 1906–1930. Liling underglaze colours paused in the 1930s and were revived after 1949 (see prc-liling).

facts.claim: After study in Japan Xiong Xiling and others founded the official Hunan Porcelain School at Liling and the next year the porcelain company, which created Liling underglaze polychrome; gold medal 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition.

sources.name: 中国博物馆协会 (relaying 广东省博物馆), 《历史的釉光——中国·清代醴陵釉下五彩瓷珍品展》 exhibition notice, 2014-04-08
sources.says: 清光绪熊希龄等人…赴日考察，归国后在醴陵创办官立湖南瓷业学堂，次年又成立瓷业公司，创烧出精美的醴陵釉下五彩瓷…1915年获得…巴拿马…金奖

sources.name: Gotheborg.com, 'Marks on Later Chinese Porcelain' (J.-E. Nilsson with Simon Ng)
sources.says: Pioneered underglaze polychrome decoration with Japanese help in the first decades of the 20th century. Modernized in 1908 and active as Hunan Porcelain Company until 1930 when it closed.

sources.name: 陈玲玲,《放逸的浅绛彩瓷》(source 《收藏家》; reprinted 景德镇名瓷在线 jdzmc.com, 2006-04-17)
sources.says: 1906年在湖南醴陵姜湾开设的“湖南瓷业公司”里的彩瓷艺人，就“多是湖南地区热爱工艺的书画名流”

facts.claim: A Hunan Museum vase is incised on the base with the Hunan Ceramics Company name and Xuantong 2nd year.

sources.name: Hunan Museum, 'Porcelain Vase with Grape Vines Design in Openwork' (collection record; text read from search-engine extract, page not reachable from here)
sources.says: The bottom of the vase is engraved with an inscription showing this piece of porcelain was created by Hunan Ceramics Company in the second year of Emperor Xuantong reign

conflicts: Founding year of school/company given as 1905 or 1906 in different sources; Gotheborg says 'modernized in 1908' and wrongly places Liling in Henan; Gotheborg has the company until 1930, a local commercial site says it was destroyed in 1918 (not used as a source).

marks.english: Yuet Tung China Works (粵東磁廠), Hong Kong, from 1928
marks.description: Printed 'Y.T.' initials with 'Decorated in Hong Kong', or the Chinese name.
marks.what_it_is: Hong Kong's oldest surviving porcelain-decorating works, founded in 1928 as Kam Wah Loong by Guangzhou guangcai masters; known for 'Rose Medallion' type export wares.
marks.dating_value: 'Y.T. Decorated in Hong Kong' marks are mostly late 20th century; the works still sells old stock, so new-old stock exists (see exp-hong-kong).

facts.claim: Founded 1928 as the Kam Wah Loong Canton porcelain factory by the Tam brothers and Tso Lui-chung, the predecessor of Yuet Tung.

sources.name: Hong Kong Memory (香港記憶), '20th Century Hong Kong Painted Porcelains—Gangcai: Arrival of Early Porcelain Practitioners in Hong Kong and their Locations of Business'
sources.says: Tam Kam-fong and Tam Kam-ping brothers, alongside Tso Lui-chung and several shareholders, pooled capital to establish the Kam Wah Loong Canton porcelain factory (the predecessor of Yuet Tung China Works) in Hong Kong in 1928.

sources.name: Victoria and Albert Museum, object record O1377000 (Hong Kong decorated porcelain, Yuet Tung)
sources.says: Yuet Tung China Works (粵東瓷廠) was established in Hong Kong in 1947, on the basis of the first porcelain factory in Hong Kong that opened in 1928.

facts.claim: Mark 'Y.T. Decorated in Hong Kong' on late-20th-century Rose Medallion plates; also 粵東磁廠 (Yue Dong Qi Chang).

sources.name: Gotheborg.com, 'Marks on Later Chinese Porcelain' (J.-E. Nilsson with Simon Ng)
sources.says: "Y.T. Decorated in Hong Kong". Modern "Rose Medallion" plate. Late 20th century … Mark: Yue Dong (Yuet Tung) Qi Chang - East Guangdong Porcelain Factory.

sources.name: Victoria and Albert Museum, object record O1377000 (Hong Kong decorated porcelain, Yuet Tung)
sources.says: Spoon … porcelain from Japan, decorated at Yuet Tung China Works, Hong Kong [mark] Y. T. Decorated in Hong Kong. Made in Japan [dated 1950s to 1960s]

conflicts: Founding: V&A (via other_marks) gives Yuet Tung 1947 on the basis of a 1928 factory; HK Memory gives 1928 for the predecessor Kam Wah Loong; a 1936 price list places Kam Wah Loong at Kak Hang Tsuen, Kowloon.
Characters: V&A writes 粵東瓷廠; the firm's name is usually written 粵東磁廠 (磁 for 瓷); Gotheborg transliterates 'Yue Dong Qi Chang'.

marks.english: A.C.F. (Ah Chow Factory), Hong Kong — 'ACF Decorated in Hong Kong' marks
marks.description: Printed English initials ACF with 'Decorated in Hong Kong', sometimes 'Japanese Porcelain Ware'.
marks.what_it_is: Hong Kong decorating factory at Tung Tau Tsuen founded by Guangzhou's Ming Kee firm, which moved its workforce to Hong Kong around 1949; its initials ACF appear on Hong Kong-decorated export wares.
marks.dating_value: 'ACF … Japanese Porcelain Ware' fits the embargo era (to 1971/72); plain ACF/AFC marks continue later.

facts.claim: A.C.F. = Ah Chow Factory ('Ah Chow' = Asia), a Hong Kong decorating company now gone.

sources.name: Victoria and Albert Museum, object record O1377000 (Hong Kong decorated porcelain, Yuet Tung)
sources.says: A.C.F. or Ah Chow Factory (Ah Chow is the Cantonese for Asia) was another company that decorated porcelain in Hong Kong that has now disappeared.

facts.claim: Guangzhou's Ming Kee evacuated its workers and assets to Hong Kong before 1949 by chartered train and set up the Ah Chow Factory at Tung Tau Tsuen.

sources.name: Hong Kong Memory (香港記憶), '20th Century Hong Kong Painted Porcelains—Gangcai: Arrival of Early Porcelain Practitioners in Hong Kong and their Locations of Business'
sources.says: Ming Kee chartered an entire Kowloon-Canton Railway through-train … established a manufacturing facility in Tung Tau Tsuen and named it as the Ah Chow Factory.

facts.claim: Marks 'ACF, Japanese Porcelain Ware, Decorated in Hong Kong' (c. 1970) and 'AFC-Decorated in Hong Kong' (last quarter 20th c.).

sources.name: Gotheborg.com, 'Marks on Later Chinese Porcelain' (J.-E. Nilsson with Simon Ng)
sources.says: Printed mark in good quality: ACF, Japanese Porcelain Ware, Decorated in Hong Kong. Date: Most likely around 1970 … "AFC-Decorated in Hong Kong", Date: Fourth quarter of 20th century.

conflicts: Gotheborg reads one mark 'AFC'; whether AFC is the same firm as ACF is not stated.

variants: JAPANESE PORCELAIN WARE DECORATED IN HONG KONG
Made in Japan / Decorated in Hong Kong
marks.english: 'JAPANESE PORCELAIN WARE · DECORATED IN HONG KONG' backstamp (1950s–1972)
marks.description: Printed English text, often with a workshop's initials (ACF, AFC, W.S.L.).
marks.what_it_is: English backstamp on Hong Kong-decorated porcelain painted on Japanese blanks, used so goods could enter the US during the embargo on Chinese goods.
marks.dating_value: Points to the Korean-War embargo era, c. 1953–72; says the blank is Japanese and the enamels were added in Hong Kong.

facts.claim: From 1953 to 1972 the US barred Chinese-made porcelain or Chinese blanks; Hong Kong decorators used Japanese blanks with a Comprehensive Certificate of Origin until Nixon's 1972 visit; backstamp 'JAPANESE PORCELAIN WARE•DECORATED IN HONG KONG•'.

sources.name: Hong Kong Memory (香港記憶), 'Gangcai: Challenges and Opportunities in the Early Development of Gangcai'
sources.says: from 1953 to 1972, the United States imposed an embargo on China … the gangcai factories universally adopted Japanese blanks … English backstamp: "JAPANESE PORCELAIN WARE•DECORATED IN HONG KONG•"

sources.name: Gotheborg.com, 'Marks on Later Chinese Porcelain' (J.-E. Nilsson with Simon Ng)
sources.says: Printed mark in good quality: ACF, Japanese Porcelain Ware, Decorated in Hong Kong. Date: Most likely around 1970.

sources.name: Victoria and Albert Museum, object record O1377000 (Hong Kong decorated porcelain, Yuet Tung)
sources.says: hence the use of marks stating that pieces were made in Japan and decorated in Hong Kong. This embargo continued until 1971. [spoon FE.5-2017 marked 'Y. T. Decorated in Hong Kong. Made in Japan', 1950s–60s]

conflicts: Embargo end: HK Memory 1972 (Nixon visit); V&A (via other_marks) 1971.

marks.english: 香港加工 'Hong Kong final process' mark (1960s–70s)
marks.description: Printed Chinese characters.
marks.what_it_is: Chinese-text mark meaning the decoration was finished in Hong Kong; the blank could be Chinese or Japanese.
marks.dating_value: 1960s–70s in Gotheborg's examples.

facts.claim: 香港加工 marks on dishes dated 1960s–1970s; decoration added in Hong Kong on Chinese or Japanese blanks.

sources.name: Gotheborg.com, 'Marks on Later Chinese Porcelain' (J.-E. Nilsson with Simon Ng)
sources.says: This mark reads 香港加工 or Xiang gang jia gong which translates to "Hong Kong Final Process" … porcelain blanks could be either Chinese or Japanese … Date 1960s to 1970s.

marks.english: 'Wah Lee Factory Made' mark, Peng Chau, Hong Kong (1953–68)
marks.description: Chinese-character factory mark without Western text (per Gotheborg); Chinese characters not given in sources.
marks.what_it_is: Mark of the Wah Lee (Wa Lee) decorating factory on Peng Chau island, Hong Kong, whose former owner dated its marked pieces to 1960.
marks.notes: The Chinese characters of the mark are not given by Gotheborg; not supplied here to avoid guessing.

facts.claim: Wa Lee Factory opened on Peng Chau in 1953 and closed in 1968; at most 80 workers; decorators trained by experts from Jingdezhen; marks dated by the owner to 1960.

sources.name: Gotheborg.com, 'Marks on Later Chinese Porcelain' (J.-E. Nilsson with Simon Ng)
sources.says: The Wa Lee Factory opened on Peng Chau Island in 1953 and closed in 1968 … at most employed 80 workers. The decorators was trained by experts having moved from Jingdezhen … Factory owner's dating: 1960.

facts.claim: Several decorating workshops operated on Peng Chau from 1953.

sources.name: Hong Kong Memory (香港記憶), '20th Century Hong Kong Painted Porcelains—Gangcai: Arrival of Early Porcelain Practitioners in Hong Kong and their Locations of Business'
sources.says: the Kwong Yee Lung factory was founded on Peng Chau island in 1953, operating alongside Chun Lung Sing and a few other cottage workshops nearby

variants: Chun Lung Sang Porcelain Company Ltd
marks.english: Chun Lung Sang (Chun Lung Sing) porcelain company, Hong Kong
marks.description: English/Chinese printed mark with company name and telephone number on later pieces.
marks.what_it_is: Hong Kong porcelain shop and decorating business; its mark appears on 1960s Hong Kong-decorated wares and, with a lead-warning label, after 1997.
marks.dating_value: Mid to late 20th century; a lead-warning label suggests 1997 or later.

facts.claim: Large shop opposite Central Market; sold in 1964 to partners including Mr Kung of Wah Lee; in Central 1965–95; lead-warning labels after a 1997 consumer report.

sources.name: Gotheborg.com, 'Marks on Later Chinese Porcelain' (J.-E. Nilsson with Simon Ng)
sources.says: Chun Lung Sang was a large shop in Central Hong Kong … In 1964 Mr. Li sold his business … It was then moved to Central, and ran there from 1965 to 1995 … In 1997 a HK Concumer Council Report

facts.claim: 'Chun Lung Sing' operated among Peng Chau cottage workshops from 1953.

sources.name: Hong Kong Memory (香港記憶), '20th Century Hong Kong Painted Porcelains—Gangcai: Arrival of Early Porcelain Practitioners in Hong Kong and their Locations of Business'
sources.says: operating alongside Chun Lung Sing and a few other cottage workshops nearby during the same period

conflicts: Gotheborg describes a shop in Shan Wan then Central; HK Memory places 'Chun Lung Sing' among Peng Chau workshops in 1953 — possibly the same firm with workshop and shop in different places.

marks.english: Kwong Yee Lung (Kwong Yee Company), Peng Chau, Hong Kong (from c. 1952–53)
marks.description: Marks not described in the sources.
marks.what_it_is: Porcelain-decorating factory on Peng Chau island, with workshops, warehouses and quarters across the island.

marks.english: Heng Hui Polychrome Porcelain (恒輝彩瓷行), Macau (1980s)
marks.description: Marks and stickers (e.g. 'decorated in Macau'); Qing reign marks (Qianlong, Jiaqing, Yongzheng) are common on Macau-decorated wares.
marks.what_it_is: The largest Macau porcelain-enamelling firm of the 1980s, with nearly 1,000 workers in Macau and a second factory in Shantou.
marks.dating_value: Macau-decorated wares are mainly 1960s–80s; Jiaqing and Tongzhi marks on such wares are decorative and late.

facts.claim: Macau's polychrome porcelain industry began in 1950, grew in the 1970s, had over 40 factories in 1981; Heng Hui employed nearly 1,000 people and ran a second factory in Shantou; exports fell sharply after 1989.

sources.name: Gotheborg.com, 'Marks on 20th century Macau porcelain' (J.-E. Nilsson; trade statistics from Chinese sources tr. David Lane)
sources.says: The first polychrome porcelain production in Macau started in 1950 … In 1981 Macau had more than 40 polychrome porcelain factories … Heng Hui Polychrome Porcelain [恒辉彩瓷行] … employed nearly 1,000 people … a second factory in Shantou

marks.english: Qing reign marks on Macau / Hong Kong-decorated wares (1960s–80s)
marks.description: Stamped or written six-character reign marks, often red, with opaque pale enamels on the body.
marks.what_it_is: Jiaqing, Tongzhi, Qianlong and Yongzheng reign marks used on porcelain made in China and enamelled in Macau or Hong Kong in the 1960s–80s.
marks.dating_value: On these wares the reign mark is decorative; style of enamels, base and stickers date them to the 1960s–80s.

facts.claim: Jiaqing marks were common in the 1960s–70s on porcelain made in China but decorated in Macao or Hong Kong; stamped Tongzhi marks were popular on Macau/Hong Kong wares in the Cultural Revolution years.

sources.name: Gotheborg.com, 'Marks on Later Chinese Porcelain' (J.-E. Nilsson with Simon Ng)
sources.says: During the 1960s to 70s this was a common mark on porelain made in China but decorated in Macao or Hong Kong … marks from the Cultural Revolution period, when Tongzhi marks enjoyed an unexplained popularity on items decorated in Macau or Hong Kong.
